consequence: The demo currently understates the product. Portfolio accuracy is 95.18% at h1 and the screen shows 78.3% with an Action badge on all four rows. Decision #78 forbids presenting an easier aggregate as SeriesKey accuracy; this is the mirror image -- the harder SeriesKey number presented against the easier portfolio target. Both are wrong, and this direction happens to harm rather than flatter, which is why it survived review.

evidence.apiReturnsLeafGrainOnly: api/internal/readmodel/forecast.go:448 queries slice_type = 'global'. That slice is sum|error| / sum(actual) over SeriesKey rows -- 78.27% at h1 on n=27,878 rows.
evidence.noAdditiveSliceExists: Every slice_type in retail_serving.forecast_metrics is leaf-grain WAPE partitioned by a dimension, not aggregate-then-difference. slice_type=market for india-west h1 is 78.57% on n=13,486 rows, which is leaf error summed within the market. The additive market figure requires summing actual and predicted to market x origin x target_week FIRST and differencing after.
evidence.uiResolvesGrainCorrectly: ui/src/Forecast.tsx:124-136 implements decision #77 first-matching-rule resolution. With All Stores and All Categories selected it correctly returns market_portfolio and correctly reads the 90/88/85/82/78 targets from the generated policy.

fix.guardrail: The new slices must be labelled by grain in the payload so decision #78 stays enforceable -- an aggregate figure must never be readable as SeriesKey accuracy.
fix.scope: no retrain required; metrics derive from existing eval predictions
steps: add market_portfolio and store_category metric slices with aggregate-then-difference semantics in the publisher metric derivation
have /api/v1/forecast/horizons carry the resolved grain and return the matching slice
have the UI request its resolved grain rather than assuming the global slice

resolution.h13StillWatch: Honest and intended. Bias is -6.3%, over the Healthy tier's 5% limit, so the long-horizon under-bias is still marked rather than papered over by the grain fix.

layers.api: readmodel/forecast.go resolves decision #77 grain server-side and aggregates actual and predicted into the grain cell before differencing. Leaf coverage is measured in the same statement and returned separately with coverageGrain=series_key, because coverage has exactly one honest grain. Payload carries metricGrain, metricSemantics and grainCells.
layers.metrics: run_artifacts.py adds market_portfolio and store_category slices computed aggregate-then-difference. Coverage is published NULL there because a sum of P90s is not the P90 of a sum -- emitting the ~1.0 that summing produces would be worse than nothing, since every decision #80 tier requires coverage inside a band and 1.0 forces Action.
layers.ui: Forecast.tsx now trusts the API metricGrain and keeps its local resolution only as a pre-response fallback. Two independent implementations of one rule set is how the mismatch arose in the first place.

resolution.noRepublishNeeded: The serving path computes additive metrics directly from forecast_eval_predictions, so the fix took effect against the already-materialized version. A later republish carrying the new metric slices produced a byte-identical version_id (fv_94f0c84a39b9f2ec) and was refused by the unique constraint -- which is correct, and is proof the change altered no served value.
resolution.testsGreen: Go all packages, ml 157 passed 2 skipped, UI 11 passed plus typecheck

rootCause: Contract and implementation diverge. forecast-health-policy.json declares metricSemantics = exact_horizon_additive, but the metric derivation only ever computed leaf-grain WAPE. Same class as the source_quality broadcast: the contract stated the correct semantics and nothing enforced them.
summary: The Forecast Health four-row table resolves its target grain correctly and then applies that target to leaf-grain numbers, because no serving metric slice implements decision #77's declared `exact_horizon_additive` semantics above SeriesKey level.
